claim: Apple's CFO explicitly attributed part of the FQ3 2026 Services growth deceleration (16% to 12% YoY) to regulatory-driven business-model changes and a US court ruling permitting external purchase links.
stance_target: contingent/regulatory-exposed earnings are already eroding reported Services growth, not merely a future risk
scope_conditions: Apple fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended June 2026), Services segment, US and unspecified 'certain countries'
quoted_support: "Let's walk from our 16% to second quarter to 12% in the June quarter, FX was the main driver in the year over year growth rates. Last year we had the theatrical release of F1, we also had some factors that impacted the App Stores, some headwinds in mobile gaming and some change to the business model in certain countries, and in the US a ruling on the link out for transactions."
entities: Epic v. Apple (implied by 'link out' ruling)

claim: Apple's EU regulatory obligations under the DMA have delayed the rollout of Apple Intelligence/Siri AI on iPhone and iPad in the EU, while Mac is exempt as a non-gatekeeper device.
stance_target: regulatory constraints materially affect Apple's product/feature rollout and hence future monetization
scope_conditions: European Union, DMA gatekeeper designation, iPhone/iPad vs Mac
quoted_support: "If you look at the EU, we're working closely with the commission. We want to launch everything, everywhere all of the time. We haven't been able to do that in the EU... it's not covered on the same regulations as the iPhone and iPad."

claim: Cook described the memory-pricing environment as a 'hundred-year flood' and said Apple reluctantly raised Mac and iPad prices due to exponential memory price increases, with no near-term end in sight.
stance_target: bear case: margin pressure from memory costs is structural, not transitory
scope_conditions: global DRAM/memory supply market, Q3-Q4 FY2026
quoted_support: "We reluctantly raised prices and because we're in a 100-year flood on the memory pricing with exponential increases in memory prices... If you look beyond September, we see the market pricing for memory continuing to increase, which could drive an increasing impact on our business."
numbers: 50.1% actual FQ3 gross margin (incl. 2pp tariff refund)

claim: Apple's FQ3 2026 revenue was $109.4 billion (+16% YoY), Services revenue $30.7 billion (+12% YoY), gross margin 50.1% (including a 2 percentage point tariff-refund benefit), and product margin 40.1%.
stance_target: baseline financial facts for the durability decomposition
quoted_support: "Company gross margin was 50.1%, up 80bp sequentially, including a benefit of tariff refunds, with an impact of 2%... Product margin was 40.1%, up 140 basis points."

claim: Apple guided FQ4 2026 total revenue growth to 9-11% YoY, down from 16% in FQ3, citing a 2.5 percentage point sequential FX headwind and supply constraints on iPhone, Mac and iPad chip nodes.
stance_target: growth deceleration is broadening beyond Services into hardware via supply constraints
quoted_support: "Expect total company revenue to grow 9-11% next quarter, and expect iPhone revenue to be impacted by foreign exchange headwinds and supply constraints... Gross margin should be between 47% and 48%."

claim: Apple's active installed base of devices surpassed 2.5 billion in FQ3 2026, reaching all-time highs across all major product categories and geographic segments.
stance_target: bull case: expanding installed base still supports Services durability
quoted_support: "Our installed base of active devices also reached a new all-time high across all major product categories and geographic segments."
